holidays.name: National Solitaire Day
holidays.description: A day for playing a game with a deck of cards and no opponent. Shuffle up, deal out the tableau, and enjoy a few quiet rounds on your own or on a screen.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It's a nod to the classic card game, which has been a favorite pastime of people playing alone for centuries.
holidays.funFact: Microsoft Solitaire came bundled with Windows 3.0 in 1990. It was meant to teach people how to use a mouse, especially dragging and dropping.

holidays.name: National Vanilla Pudding Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate smooth, creamy, spoonable comfort. Eat it plain, layer it in a banana pudding, or dollop it on cake.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It celebrates one of the most beloved classic desserts.
holidays.funFact: Vanilla comes from the pods of an orchid. Real vanilla beans are among the most labor-intensive and expensive spices in the world, second in price only to saffron.

holidays.name: Sherlock Holmes Day
holidays.description: A day for deerstalker hats, magnifying glasses, and deducing things about strangers. Fans mark it by rereading the stories or watching their favorite detective adaptation.
holidays.origin: It falls on the birthday of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, who was born on May 22, 1859. He created the famously observant detective of 221B Baker Street.
holidays.funFact: Holmes never says "Elementary, my dear Watson" in the original Conan Doyle stories. The famous line came from later adaptations.
